Chapter 6. The Aftermath—A Family Torn Apart.
When the guillotine finally falls and the crowd fades away, life doesn’t just pick up where it left off. The echoes of that day don’t disappear—they linger, heavy and sharp, in the hearts of everyone left behind.
Picture the Temple prison, its shadowy rooms now holding Marie Antoinette’s children and her sister-in-law. Suddenly, everything they once knew is gone. The monarchy’s finished, but for this family, the pain of loss is just starting to take hold.
Imagine the queen’s son—a boy who, not long ago, was the hope of a whole dynasty. Now, he’s scared and alone, torn away from his family and completely at the mercy of his captors. Outside those walls, people argue over his fate. But inside? He’s just a child, desperate for his mother’s arms. His older sister tries to protect him, to soothe his fears, but she’s carrying her own heartbreak. The adults who are left do what little they can, but their influence is gone. They’re powerless, watching as everything they loved slips away.
And what about those who once served the royal family? For them, every day is a careful balancing act—trying to survive in a world that’s turned upside down. Some choose to forget, blending in, hoping no one remembers their loyalty. Others can’t let go, risking everything just to honor the past. Even the city feels different now. The streets that used to echo with grand royal parades are filled instead with revolutionary songs. People themselves have changed, too. Some are relieved, some feel regret, but most are just doing their best to get by.
Far away in Vienna, Marie Antoinette’s family mourns from a distance. Letters go back and forth, full of longing and sorrow, but words can’t bridge the gap or undo what’s happened. The empress—who once planned every detail of her daughter’s life—is gone. The siblings left behind are haunted by questions. Could any of this have been different? That sense of helplessness runs deep.
When most people face tragedy, they turn to routine or lean on loved ones for comfort. But for the remnants of the royal family, even those simple comforts are out of reach. Their world has vanished. The future? It’s a blank page, full of uncertainty.
Yet, in those rare and quiet moments—when they share a story, or whisper a prayer—there’s a spark of hope. Maybe, just maybe, something of what they lost can be remembered. Even if it can’t be restored, it lives on in memory.
